scope: Choosing the PDF engine for Aizome's reader (Shiori): PDFium against hayro, the permissively licensed candidates, over the pdf.js test corpus; then Shiori's own worker over the same corpus. Component evidence on one laptop; not VM, ISO or hardware qualification.
workstation: ganymede (8 threads, 30 GiB RAM); other agents' builds shared it (one-minute load average 6-11)

corpus.source: https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js test/pdfs (the PDFs in the repository, not the linked ones)
corpus.note: Deliberately hostile: many files are reduced bug reports, fuzzer output and broken on purpose. Rates here are not real-world failure rates.

excluded.pdf.js: Apache-2.0, but JavaScript: it needs a web engine, not a native renderer
excluded.lopdf: MIT; reads and writes PDF syntax, does not draw pages

compared.PDFium: BSD-3-Clause and Apache-2.0 (nixpkgs meta: asl20, bsd3, mit); nixpkgs `pdfium` 8066 built from source with gn, system FreeType, libjpeg, OpenJPEG, lcms2, libpng, libtiff, zlib, HarfBuzz and ICU; V8, XFA and PartitionAlloc off; libpdfium.so 4.8 MiB; substituted from cache.nixos.org
compared.pdfium-render 0.9.4: MIT OR Apache-2.0; bindings to PDFium's API up to build 7881, loaded at run time
compared.hayro 0.8.0: Apache-2.0 OR MIT; pure Rust, forbids unsafe code in the rasterizer; default features (embedded standard fonts and CMaps)

method.program: a scratch benchmark (not in the tree): each file in a process of its own under `timeout 30`, four at a time, release build; up to the first 5 pages rendered at 2x (144 dpi) on white, PDFium with forms and annotations; time per page includes loading (parsing) the page
method.comparison: per page, the largest per-channel difference of each pixel; a pixel differs when that exceeds 48 of 255; renders compared where both engines drew the page at the same size (within 2 px)

crashes.jpx_numcomps.pdf: exit 133 (SIGTRAP): one of PDFium's own checks stopping the process

pdfium_right: knockout_blend_multiply (hayro has no knockout groups or this blend)
hayro_right: jpx_subsampling (PDFium drew one of several JPEG 2000 images)
calgray (hayro converts CalGray colorimetrically; PDFium treats it as DeviceGray)
same_but_antialiasing: tracemonkey page 5 (5.2% of pixels differ, indistinguishable by eye)

features_a_reader_needs.pdfium: text with character boxes, search with result rectangles, links and destinations, the outline, AcroForm drawing (and filling), annotations, metadata and permissions, passwords (RC4 and AES)
features_a_reader_needs.hayro: drawing, and passwords; text, search, links and the outline would be built on its syntax and interpreter crates

decision: PDFium, in a worker process of its own per document: equal speed on the median page, a far shorter tail, the reader's features, and the failures above contained to a page. hayro is the alternative to watch: memory-safe and already close on compatibility.

shiori_worker_over_the_corpus.tested_source: branch aizome-pdf-reader (Shiori's first version), release build
shiori_worker_over_the_corpus.method: apps/shiori/examples/corpus.rs, four files at a time: open; draw a 1024 px tile of each of the first 3 pages at 1.5x the 868-point width; their text and links; search 'the' over the first 10 pages
shiori_worker_over_the_corpus.recovery: in each stopped or crashed case a new worker opened the document again; the harness doesn't ask again after that (the app does, which tests/shiori.rs covers)
